title: On the shelf is not all free
hook: Six units are promised. Can every unit on the shelf serve a new request?

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Separate physical inventory from uncommitted availability.

misconception: Every item physically present is available for a new request.
objective: Separate physical inventory from uncommitted availability.

claims.text: Six on-shelf units are already committed to earlier requests. Compare free and physical counts. Scaled model; six committed; no incoming stock.
claims.source: Declared hypothetical inputs and limits in resource-specs.json. No actual product, price, tariff, shelf-life, treatment or physical appliance specification is asserted. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: The stage's two results are computed by the printed expressions. At On-shelf=10, A=4items and B=10items. Geometry follows the declared dimension relationships. Other pictures use a fixed full scale across the slider range; continuous fills and arcs show relative amounts rather than literal object counts.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["max",0,["-","x",6]]; B="x"; x denotes On-shelf. At x=10, A=4, B=10. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. Diagram scale: resourceGraphicScale in resource-model.ts takes the maximum modeled magnitude across both formulas and the declared slider range. For non-geometry figures, full-scale values are displayed; the scale stays fixed when the slider changes. Energy axis endpoints use resourceAxisEnd, including B=5×A hours in lh-watts-hours-trade; cylinder rx and ry both scale with radius in resourceCylinderDimensions. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: Subtract committed units from the physical count to find free units. Commitments do not make the objects disappear, but they change which requests those objects can satisfy.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["max",0,["-","x",6]]; B="x"; x denotes On-shelf. At x=10, A=4, B=10. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. The principle follows from those expressions and stated scenario limits. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: Fifteen units are on the shelf and nine are already promised to earlier requests. How many can a new request take? Correct: 6. Free units are physical minus committed: 15 − 9 = 6. The promised units are present but not available.
